recent_posts.title: 11 GEO tools compared for improving AI search visibility in 2026
recent_posts.summary: A curated comparison of 11 generative engine optimization (GEO) tools for improving brand visibility in AI-generated answers from ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and similar engines. Tools are categorized into three types: content production tools (Frase, Writesonic), monitoring/tracking tools (Goodie AI, Peec AI, Rankscale AI, GetCito, AthenaHQ, Profound AI, SE Ranking), and full-stack platforms that close the measure-act-publish loop (HeyAmos). Each tool is evaluated on features, pros, cons, and pricing. A buying framework helps teams choose based on their maturity level, team size, and whether they need monitoring only or end-to-end execution.

recent_posts.title: Top developer tools and practices for social media API privacy in 2026
recent_posts.summary: A guide covering architectural privacy flaws in social platforms and how developers can address them. Topics include API vulnerability exposure, broken object-level authorization, metadata harvesting, and shadow profiling. Practical solutions include zero-trust architecture, TLS 1.3, OAuth 2.0, data minimization, and regular third-party SDK audits. Also reviews five security auditing tools: OWASP ZAP, SonarQube, Postman, Snyk, and Burp Suite Professional, with pros and cons for each.

recent_posts.title: How to Build a JSON Training Dataset from PDF Documents Without Manual Annotation
recent_posts.summary: A complete Python pipeline for converting PDF documents into structured JSON training datasets without manual annotation. Covers PDF extraction library selection (PyMuPDF, pdfplumber, unstructured), token-aware chunking strategies, LLM-based QA pair generation using OpenAI's API, programmatic validation to catch hallucinations, embedding-based deduplication, and multi-turn conversation data generation. Includes benchmark results across legal, technical, and research document types showing costs as low as $3–5 per 5,000 examples versus $2,500–4,000 for human annotation. Also discusses dataset format choices (Alpaca, ShareGPT, ChatML) and when automated generation should be supplemented with human review.

recent_posts.title: How to Name Your App (and Get the Best Trademark)
recent_posts.summary: Naming an app requires more than creativity — it demands strategic thinking about trademark protection, brand identity, and long-term defensibility. The post walks through a naming framework covering how to position your app before brainstorming, the spectrum of name types from generic to fanciful and their trademark strength, early availability checks (domain, app stores, social handles), and how to properly register a trademark. Common pitfalls like choosing overly descriptive names or skipping legal research are highlighted, along with the distinction between trademarking a brand name versus copyrighting an app idea.

recent_posts.title: 7 WordPress and web design tools for faster workflows in 2026
recent_posts.summary: A curated list of seven WordPress and web design tools for 2026, covering AI-powered website builders, lightweight themes, WooCommerce-focused themes, and animation plugins. Featured products include Mobirise AI (no-code AI builder), Blocksy, WoodMart, Uncode, Slider Revolution 7, Crafto, and XStore, each reviewed with key strengths, use cases, and user ratings.

recent_posts.title: The Model Handshake: Chaining AI Agents for Complex Refactors
recent_posts.summary: Single-prompt AI refactoring fails at scale due to context window limits and coherence degradation. The 'model handshake' pattern solves this by chaining specialized AI agents (Analyst, Architect, Implementer, Reviewer) where each stage consumes a validated JSON schema from the previous stage and produces a schema-conformant output for the next. The post covers full architecture design, handoff contract schemas, a Python orchestration script using Claude and GPT-4o, validation gates with Pydantic and jsonschema, retry/error-recovery strategies, and a real-world walkthrough migrating a 40-file Express.js API to Fastify. Limitations include overhead for small refactors, multiplied API costs, and inherent non-determinism.

recent_posts.title: Next.js AI Streaming: Building Real-Time Apps with Vercel AI SDK
recent_posts.summary: Step-by-step guide to building a real-time AI chat application using Next.js App Router, Vercel AI SDK 4.x, and React Suspense. Covers scaffolding the project, creating an edge-compatible streaming API route with streamText and Zod validation, building a client-side chat UI with the useChat hook, integrating React Suspense for server-fetched chat history, and advanced patterns including structured output with streamObject, multi-step tool calling, edge vs Node.js runtime trade-offs, caching strategies, and a production readiness checklist covering security, accessibility, and error handling.

recent_posts.title: Claude Code vs Cursor vs Copilot: The 2026 Developer Comparison
recent_posts.summary: A practical comparison of Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot in 2026, benchmarked against the same React component refactoring task. All three tools are tested on multi-file editing, agentic autonomy, context handling, pricing, model flexibility, and team collaboration. Claude Code completed all 8 files autonomously and ran a lint check without follow-up prompts, excelling at terminal-native complex refactors with a 200K token context window. Cursor offered the best visual diff workflow with inline accept/reject controls in an AI-native IDE. Copilot required more manual file management but remains the pragmatic choice for GitHub-embedded teams with mature enterprise controls and multi-model flexibility. The verdict: no single winner — many developers combine Claude Code for deep refactors with Copilot for daily completions.

recent_posts.title: MCP Model Context Protocol: Complete Developer Integration Guide
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive step-by-step guide to building a full MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration stack. Covers creating a Python MCP server using FastMCP with custom tools and resources, setting up a Node.js Express bridge that connects to the server via SSE transport and exposes REST endpoints, and building a React frontend that dynamically discovers and invokes tools from JSON Schema. Also addresses testing with MCP Inspector, common pitfalls like CORS and schema mismatches, and production considerations including security, authentication, and performance.

recent_posts.title: AI Agent Testing Automation: Developer Workflows for 2026
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to building a testing harness for AI agents in Node.js. Covers deterministic unit testing via LLM mocking with dependency injection, Zod schema validation for structural correctness, a batch evaluation runner with fixture-based scoring and a 90% pass-rate CI gate, GitHub Actions integration, and a React dashboard for visualizing eval results. Also discusses emerging trends like multi-agent testing, standardization tools (OpenAI Evals, LangSmith, Braintrust), and autonomous test generation.
